references.text: Moses goes out from Pharaoh and prays to the Lord, a similar pattern where Moses intercedes after a plague
Moses leaves Pharaoh and cries out to the Lord, the same pattern of intercession during the plagues
Moses goes out from Pharaoh and prays to the Lord to remove the locusts, a parallel pattern
Moses intercedes for the people before the Lord, showing Moses' role as mediator
The people ask Moses to pray to the Lord to take away the snakes, a similar intercession situation
Samuel cries out to the Lord for Israel, prophetic intercession similar to Moses' intercession
Samuel cries out to the Lord, parallel to Moses crying out to God in crisis situations
Elijah is mentioned as an example of effective intercession; Moses' intercession had the same power
Chronological and theological contrast: God's command to send the plague (v5) versus Moses' prayer to remove it (v8).
Contrast between Moses' prayer to remove the plague and Pharaoh's admission of sin and plea for help.
Parallel in the dynamics of conflict: Moses' prayer to remove judgment versus Pharaoh's admission of guilt during another plague.
